spatial_claims.claim: BC and CG are placed in one straight line BG with C between B and G
D and E lie on opposite sides of line BG
DC stands on line BG at C, so adjacent angles BCD + DCG = two right angles (1.13)
Angles ECG + DCG = two right angles (since angle ECG = angle BCD, adding DCG to both sides)
CD and CE lie on opposite sides of line CG, with angles DCG + GCE = two right angles, so CE is in a straight line with DC by 1.14; the line is called DE
DH is parallel to CG and GH is parallel to CD; they meet at H forming parallelogram DCGH
Parallelograms AC (=ABCD) and CH (=DCGH) have bases BC, CG on line BG and share the same height (perpendicular from D to BG)
Parallelograms CH (=DCGH) and CF (=CEFG) have bases DC, CE on line DE and share the same height (perpendicular from G to DE)

configuration_map: Point C: shared vertex of parallelograms ABCD, CEFG, and bridging parallelogram DCGH, at the intersection of lines BG and DE. Points B, G: on a horizontal line through C with C between them; B is a vertex of ABCD, G is a vertex of CEFG. Point D: vertex of ABCD on one side of line BG; also a vertex of DCGH. Point E: vertex of CEFG on the opposite side of line BG from D; collinear with D and C (D-C-E is a straight line, proved in Step 5). Point H: fourth vertex of parallelogram DCGH, on the same side of BG as D, constructed as the intersection of the line through D parallel to CG with the line through G parallel to CD. Parallelogram AC (=ABCD): base BC on line BG, opposite side AD parallel to BG at height equal to perpendicular distance from D to BG. Parallelogram CH (=DCGH): base CG on line BG and base DC on line DE; acts as the bridging parallelogram. Parallelogram CF (=CEFG): base CE on line DE, with G on line BG at perpendicular distance from line DE equal to the height of CH measured from G.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction is a standard placement of equiangular parallelograms at a shared vertex C, with sides BC-CG made collinear and D-C-E proved collinear via supplementary angles and I.14. The bridging parallelogram DCGH correctly shares a base line and height with each original parallelogram, enabling two valid applications of VI.1. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside point-position claims, and no betweenness contradictions arise. The proof follows the same geometric logic as Heath's but more directly, omitting auxiliary proportional lines.
